$comment: #2458 — THE shared cross-language parity fixture for the Commercial buyer-subtype mapping.
Two implementations exist because the mapping is needed on both sides of the language
That duplication is unavoidable; leaving it UNCHECKED is not.
Both sides assert against THIS file. A change to either implementation alone makes that
side's test fail, which is the whole point — neither side's own suite can detect one-sided
drift, because each proves only that it is self-consistent.
INPUTS ARE CANONICAL BY CONTRACT. propertyType is the stored lower-case token; subtype is
the stored UPPER-case value or null. Casing normalisation is a SEPARATE concern and is
covered separately on each side — Java by normalizeCommercialSubtype in the shared
buildListing funnel plus UPPER() on the column in the predicate, TypeScript inside the
resolver itself. Mixing it in here would put two different contracts under one fixture.
null expected values are HONEST ABSENCE, never a guess, and carry two distinct cases the
caller separates using propertyType — which is NOT NULL and always correct. See the

cases.name: shop
cases.why: the ambiguous family, disambiguated by the subtype axis

cases.name: office
cases.why: the other half of the only pair property_type alone cannot separate

cases.name: legacy-generic-commercial
cases.why: V102 hardcodes NULL because shop-vs-office is unrecoverable from legacy data; inferring either would fabricate it. Renders the generic Commercial branch, selected by propertyType.

cases.name: commercial-building-self-describing
cases.why: self-describing types resolve from propertyType ALONE — this is what keeps legacy Building rows visible despite carrying no subtype on any read axis

cases.name: warehouse-self-describing
cases.why: same; a subtype-only resolver would return null here and lose the row

cases.name: self-describing-type-ignores-a-conflicting-subtype
cases.why: property_type is NOT NULL and authoritative for the self-describing types; a stray subtype value must not override it, or the two sides could disagree on precedence

cases.name: non-commercial
cases.why: not a commercial row at all — the OTHER null case, separated by propertyType

cases.name: non-commercial-with-stray-subtype
cases.why: an apartment is not a shop; neither side may promote a stray subtype into a peer

cases.name: null-property-type
cases.why: defensive: the column is NOT NULL, but both implementations accept nullable input and must agree on it
